identity_evidence.quote: A 23-year-old male with autoimmune uveitis and a family history of multiple sclerosis (MS) developed two neurological attacks, after Adalimumab infusion

attribution_limitations: The neurological examination is called normal except for the pupillary abnormality, but the next sentence lists further abnormal findings that were also noticed.

The diagnosis is worded as Adalimumab induced MS (suspected), as induced or provoked MS (most likely diagnosis) and as a process that suggests uncovering latent MS rather than inducing it; the authors do not choose between them.
Certainty of the uveitis type differs: hints of anterior and intermediate uveitis in the case presentation, revealed both anterior and intermediate uveitis in the Discussion.
Infectious causes and lymphoma are called improbable, and the X-rays were requested to rule out subclinical ankylosing spondylitis and sarcoidosis; none of these is stated as excluded or confirmed.

Several statements describe an MRI without active lesions or disease (repeated MRI with no new lesions; no active lesions on MRI; MRI performed six months later with no active disease) and the source does not state that they are the same study.
Figure 1 is cited for the first MRI and Figure 2 for the repeated MRI; neither caption states a time, and the caption findings (Flair and T2 slices) are recorded separately from the text findings.

The report gives no calendar dates. "A year ago" has no named reference point, "Six months after then" and "since then" are unanchored, and the second attack is anchored to the Adalimumab infusion in the case presentation but to halting Adalimumab in the Discussion.

The Discussion speaks of the first and second clinical attack; the case presentation describes right hemibody anesthesia and right lower limb paresis without calling them attacks 1 and 2, and the abstract says the attacks occurred simultaneously with cerebral lesions on MRI.
The HLA-B27 association of the uveitis is stated flatly in the case presentation and the Discussion opening but the uveitis type is later called more compatible with HLA-B27 uveitis.
The case text prints the allele as HLAB-27 in one sentence and HLA-B27 elsewhere; "AXR of the pelvis" is not stated to be the same study as the X-ray of sacroiliac joints.
